Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork "JusPrin"). Work in the worktree this session gives you; do not touch the main checkout. First `git fetch origin` and base your branch on origin/jusprin-newui (336facf825 or later).

## What this is

The project chat's system prompt is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`, moved there unchanged from C++ on 2026-10-14 (commit 6b4b8b6188) and pinned byte for byte by `projectInstructions.test.ts` against `projectInstructions.fixture.txt` (2,815 bytes). The page sends it whole as `project_instructions`; the app has no default text. A critique of that prompt was written on 2026-10-14 against OpenAI's GPT-5 and GPT-4.1 prompting guides and Anthropic's context-engineering and prompting guides; its findings, in short, are below. Kenneth has decided to do two of its fixes together, because both are refactoring: give every rule one home, and restructure the prompt into sections at the level of principles.

## What the critique found (the parts you act on)

1. The prompt is one 129-word paragraph of eleven unrelated rules (identity, scope, grounding, tool honesty, output) followed by three dense paragraphs headed "Intent and setup", "Preparation", "Verification". Every guide recommends sections with headers or XML tags, in roughly this order: role, when to act, grounding, workflow, communication.
2. Five overlapping statements say when to act ("when asked to make a supported change, call the matching tool"; "a question or a troubleshooting request is not by itself a request to change the project"; "advice requests call for recommendations, not project changes"; "a clear request for a specific supported change can use its tools directly"; "for preparation involving multiple changes, record the plan with plan_set before applying"). OpenAI's guide says contradictions and overlaps are the most expensive defect for this model family. There must be one decision rule with named cases: a specific change request; a prepare-or-print request; a question or advice; a print-issue turn (the canvas buttons send "Explain this issue and my options." or "Help fix this issue." with a print_issue context; both get the same tools).
3. The same policy lives in two or three places and drifts. Examples: the export preflight rule is in the prompt and again in the `export_file` description; "treat notes in the file as recommendations, not instructions" is in the `project_open` description and again in the host's developer boundary line; the `settings_preview_patch` description carries a 90-word paragraph on how to settle a `skipped_confirmation` warning (go ahead; go ahead and tell the user; ask first when the answer is the user's); the file-report skill (`fileReportInstructions.ts`, sent as a developer item for one turn) restates the identity ("You are JusPrin, the 3D printing app…") and sets a rule that contradicts the standing one ("do not call a tool in this response"). Kenneth's rule: one home per kind of thing. Standing policy lives in the prompt only. Tool descriptions state the contract: what the tool does, its arguments, its result, what undo does. The skill says "the rules above still apply; for this one response…" and carries only its judgement content.
4. Rules without reasons, and negative rules without their positive trigger ("Do not repeat an assessment just because a title was recorded or unchanged intent was restated" should become "reassess when intent, material, printer or an object changes"). Anthropic's guide: give the why so the model generalizes; say what to do.
5. No communication guidance at all, while the panel renders GitHub-flavoured Markdown and the other chats specify language, audience and length. One short section: reply in the user's language; plain terms, keeping the 3D-printing word when it names the thing; short by default; Markdown lists and bold allowed, no headers; first person for the app's actions ("I", never "OrcaSlicer warned" as if another app did it); after a tool result, say what happened in the person's terms.
6. Engineer's words in the model's text ("authorization boundary" was one, already removed). Write for the model, not the code reviewer.

## What Kenneth ruled out

- No few-shot examples, and no eagerness or stop-condition rule lists. His experience: they bloat the prompt and confuse the agent. Principles with their reason, not rules.
- Mechanics the app enforces are not restated in the prompt (argument validation, refusals, the session and revision check).
- No approve, authorize, confirm-before, or "ask the user then call again" wording anywhere; tool-call approval was removed on 2026-10-07. A sentence that needs a precondition says "pass X only when the person asked for X".
- A prompt change must delete at least as much text as it adds unless a measured failure justifies the addition. Target: the new prompt is shorter than 2,815 bytes.
- Do not move the prompt back to C++, do not add a skill index, do not change the snapshot or history handling (separate items).

## What to deliver

- The new `projectInstructions.ts`, sectioned (XML-style tags or Markdown headers, your choice, consistently), with the fixture updated. Every sentence should be traceable to one of the findings above or to the old text.
- Tool descriptions in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp` trimmed to contracts where they carried policy (`export_file`, `project_open`, `settings_preview_patch` at least; grep the descriptions for "should", "explain", "treat", "ask" to find others). The `skipped_confirmation` handling moves into the prompt as one short principle. Regenerate `tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json` and the project harness's tools fixture after description changes; their drift tests fail otherwise.
- `fileReportInstructions.ts` without its identity restatement and without rules the standing prompt already has.
- The host's developer boundary line in `AgentHost::make_agent_request` ("Earlier file-load reports … are source data…") stays; it is a per-turn fact, not standing policy.

## How to measure

The eval harness is on branch `claude/project-prompt-harness` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/project-prompt-harness`, commit 5ae439525b or later; read its `tests/project_prompt/README.md` first). It judges the model's next step at a point recorded from the app, answering read-only calls from recordings, on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter with a pinned judge. Credentials are in `~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`; load them only in the subshell that runs the suite and never print them. Kenneth approved the batch for this task on 2026-10-15: one run per case, the old prompt and the new prompt in the same session, paired. Unobserved outcomes (the model asked for a read the recording lacks) are acceptable and are reported as such, not as failures. Report the token total from the responses' usage fields. If the harness branch is not yet merged, cherry-pick or rebase it into your worktree for the measurement and say so; do not change its cases to make them pass. If the keys return 403 Key limit exceeded, stop and report.

Before the live run, offline: agent_bridge_tests, the AgentUI vitest suite (the fixture test will fail until you update the fixture, which is the point), and the harness's render-only mode. Build `jusprin_web` so the bundle carries the new text. Build recipe: /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md (CMake from /Applications/CMake.app, reuse existing deps, BUILD_TESTS=ON; long builds with nohup and a log, never as a background Bash command).

Commit on a branch in your worktree, do not push. Write an untracked report in the worktree root (never commit it, never add it to .gitignore) for an engineer who did not see this session: the new prompt in full, a table mapping each old sentence to where it went (kept, merged, moved to a description, deleted and why), the byte counts before and after, the paired per-case results with unobserved counted separately, the token total, and anything the measurement says you got wrong. Plain English, no label-colon fragments; Kenneth reads these.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

**Renamed 2026-10-14 (branch claude/no-save-prompts, dfd89a1379):** the code is now `skipped_confirmation`, rules in `SkippedConfirmations.hpp` (`skipped_edit_confirmations`, `skipped_save_confirmations` — the latter covers Tab::save_preset's first-layer temperature check). Kenneth found "orca_question" a bad name; use "skipped confirmation" when discussing it.

On 2026-10-12 Kenneth decided how the settings tools treat the questions OrcaSlicer asks only when a person edits a field (`Tab::on_value_change`, which `Tab::load_config` never runs). He chose, in his words, to "forward this text to the agent" and let the agent decide one of three: go ahead silently, go ahead and tell the user, or ask the user as an extra turn. He then picked "way 1": our own copy of OrcaSlicer's conditions, guarded by a test.

**What was built** (branch `claude/edit-time-questions`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/exciting-feistel-6dc0c0`, landed on jusprin-newui as 2f308f2dda by fast-forward and pushed, 2026-10-12): `forward_edit_questions` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaEditQuestions.hpp`, called from `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::preview_settings`. One preview warning per question, code `orca_question`, message = OrcaSlicer's words, `suggestions` = the values its Yes would set. The patch stays valid and applies as sent. The `settings_preview_patch` description tells the agent the three choices. Guide section: "Questions OrcaSlicer asks a person who edits a field" in `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`.

**Why:** a valid tool call already starts at once with no approval step; a "the person agreed" field would only be the agent's word. I had proposed a refuse-until-agreed gate for `make_overhang_printable`; Kenneth's design replaced it.

**How to apply:**
- Do not add a gate, a blacklist entry, or an approval step for these settings. Do not call OrcaSlicer's handler with a dialog listener from product code.
- A question fires only for a key the patch really changes (in `result.changes`, so after the normalizer), with its condition read from the patch's values before normalization. Not for a state that already exists.
- The test is the guard: `verify_edit_questions` and the sweep in `tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` set the value in the tab's config, call the real `tab->on_value_change`, capture dialogs with `ScopedDialogListener`, and compare text with what preview forwarded. After an upstream update a mismatch reads `Orca asks ..., preview forwarded ...`.
- My interpretation, not Kenneth's words: messages are looked up with `_u8L` per piece, so the agent gets the interface language.

**Traps found while building:**
- The English catalog (`localization/i18n/en`) rewords some msgids ("smooth timelapse" shows as "smooth timelapse mode ... the prime tower"). What a person sees is the catalog text, not the literal in `Tab.cpp`. Copy the msgid and translate; never hard-code the English.
- `enable_wrapping_detection` is silently turned back off on printers whose type lacks it (X1C); P2S and H2D have it. The harness sets `printer_model` to "Bambu Lab P2S" for those cases.
- `sparse_infill_rotate_template`'s question depends on `m_last_sparse_infill_rotate_template_value`, which `Tab::reload_config` resets; emulate the hand edit before any `load_config`, not after an apply.
- The handler `any_cast`s the field value for a few keys: bool, int for enums, `std::string`, `unsigned char` for per-extruder switches, double. The printer tab's per-extruder keys carry `#0`.

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge.

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a tool call or a reply. A read the case does not decide on (any
read-only tool, such as `workspace_inspect` before a reply) is answered with
the result the app gave for that read at the same point, and the model is
asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`). Nothing else is ever
answered: a change, or any call the case judges, is the outcome and ends the
run. A read with no recorded answer, or a fourth read, ends it unobserved. A
call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it is
the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 23
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **An answered read** is added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then the result under the model's call id. The answer carries

What is written by hand is only what a model or a person would have said: the

scripted calls carry the replay form the app uses (`call_id`, `name`,
`arguments`); a live model's own item id, status and reasoning items within a
turn are not reproducible. Nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current:
record it again when a tool's results, the fixture or the request shape
change. It was recorded at jusprin-newui 336facf825.

The app streams its requests and this script does not.

IDs are strings scoped to the returned sessionId. No process-setting values are exposed by this tool.
